# Introduction {#sec-intro}

Language models routinely act on information they have not written down: a model
completing a couplet selects its rhyme before writing the line that ends in it
[@lindsey2025biology; @hanna2026latent], and a model asked for a calculation or a secret
choice must hold or reconstruct that content across the tokens it writes in between. How
such information reaches the position that uses it matters for chain-of-thought
monitoring, which assumes that decision-relevant reasoning passes through, or can be
recovered from, the text the model writes [@korbak2025monitorability;
@baker2025monitoring]. The central risk to that assumption is content the model uses but
never states [@pfau2024dots; @roger2023steganography; @turpin2023unfaithful;
@chen2025reasoning].

In a transformer, information at one position can reach a later position in three ways
(@fig-overview). It can be **emitted**: it changes the tokens the model writes, which
are read back as input. It can be **looked up**: read from a fixed position of the
context, where it originates or in visible text from which it can be recomputed. Or it can be **relayed**: the hidden states of the generated positions pick it up and pass it on, although the words written there do not express it. Emitted information is in the text and looked-up information stays at a fixed position of the context, where it can be read or probed; relay is the path by which a model could hold content across a chain of thought that never states it. Lookup turns out to have a
second site: a **stored copy**, written once into a structural position of the prompt
next to the source. Prior work decodes upcoming tokens from hidden states [@pal2023futurelens] and locates
where plans are formed or can be steered [@lindsey2025biology; @hanna2026latent;
@maar2026plan], but does not measure how much of a plan's effect takes each path to
where it is used.

![Route accounting on a rhyme plan. The paths by which a plan formed at the rhyme word
of line 1 (where the donor state is written) reaches the position that predicts the
rhyme, with the line-2 words held fixed. Widths are each path's measured share of
persistence in Qwen3-32B with the chat prompt: most of the plan is read directly from the
rhyme word, and relay through the hidden states of line 2 accounts for 1%. Appendix @fig-overview-points gives, for every setting and model, the looked-up share and the share of relay or of an unsplit indirect path.](manuscript/figures/iclr_fig1_overview.png){#fig-overview width=100% fig-pos="t"}

We introduce **route accounting** (@sec-method). A donor's hidden states are written at
the source positions, and the effect is measured where the information is used. Fixing
the generated text separates emission from persistence. Clamping the states of chosen
groups of positions, at every layer, separates direct retrieval of the source from
indirect paths through intermediate positions, which we split by position into the stored copy, the late lookup just before the target, and relay through the rest of the generated text. Direct retrieval, the stored copy and the late lookup all read the information from a fixed prompt position, so they are the three forms of lookup; relay is the only path that holds it across the generated text. On induction [@olsson2022induction], where the known mechanism passes information through the hidden state at the position of a copied token, route accounting finds that indirect
path as the largest path in all nine models tested (@sec-control).

Applied to four tasks in 15 checkpoints from three model families, route accounting finds
one principle, within the settings tested (short generated spans, thinking disabled):
**look it up, don't carry it**. Models read unwritten information near the point of use
from a fixed position of the prompt, the source or a copy stored next to it, rather than relay it through the hidden states of the text they generate (@tbl-map; @sec-lookup). Rhyme plans are read
mainly from the rhyme word (68 to 95% of persistence in all but one configuration), and relay accounts for at most 1% in all 21 runs. Donor states at
every position after a computed value's source move the answer by at most 4.9% (variable
chains) and 6.4% (sums) of the source effect, while written intermediate values are
followed: emission accounts for at least 83% of the effect.

Three stress tests with committed decision rules make relay useful or the content
invisible (@sec-stress). Beyond Gemma 3's attention window, Gemma 3 27B hands the plan from the rhyme word to the
stored copy, and the generated text accounts for 9 to 13%, not split into late lookup
and relay. In a recurrent hybrid, entry through the recurrent layers produces 2 to 4% of
persistence. A secret choice is stored at a few low-content prompt tokens, and at most 2% of its effect passes through the hidden states of the intervening sentence. The one path that grows is the stored
copy: it appears at 14B and above in Qwen3 and at 12B to 27B in Gemma 3, is present in
base checkpoints, and reconciles published accounts of where the rhyme plan lives.

**Contributions.** (1) Route accounting, a position-level decomposition of intervention effects into emission, lookup and relay, validated on a positive control. (2) The principle that unwritten information is looked up, not relayed, across
tasks, families, sizes, prompt formats, checkpoints and intervention types. (3) Three
stress tests with committed decision rules that bound it. (4) A stored copy that emerges
with scale, reconciling published accounts of rhyme planning.

Where unwritten information travels: the share of the effect by path, as a range over
the models tested, of persistence unless stated. *Looked up*: the target reads the source,
a copy stored at a structural token next to it, or the late lookup. *Relay, or an unsplit indirect path*: relay where it was separated (rhyme plans);
otherwise the named group of intermediate positions. *Visible* content can be recovered by
a reader of the text; *hidden* content cannot. Dashes mark cells the design rules out. A
share above 100% means that the other paths, or their interaction, are negative.
The sections and appendix give the full results with 95% intervals.

:::
